subject: maths
title: Roots of Unity and Geometric Uses
welcome_lead: Find the n equally spaced roots of unity and apply them geometrically.
meta_desc: HL Maths adventure on nth roots of unity and geometric applications.
final_note: n roots of unity sit on a unit circle, evenly spaced!

concepts.def: ω = e^(2πi/n), generates all n roots.
Sum of all nth roots of unity is 0 (n ≥ 2).
Vertices of regular n-gon on unit circle.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Find fourth roots of 16.

r = 16^(1/4) = 2; angles 0, π/2, π, 3π/2; so z = 2, 2i, -2, -2i.

5th roots of unity form regular pentagon.

Vertices at e^(2πik/5), k = 0.4 on |z| = 1.

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
They add up to 180 degrees.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.
Yes, because the 2 represents how many times x appears.
8xy, by combining all terms regardless of variable.
They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
5x + 3y — combine like terms (3x + 2x and 4y - y).
9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.

mcqs.q: Is 2x the same as x squared (x^2)?
options: No — 2x means x + x (or 2 times x); x^2 means x times x.
They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
Yes, because both involve the number 2 and the letter x.
Yes, because the 2 represents how many times x appears.
